rationale: The Sinatra app only calls send_file; there is no exception, just a worker pinned at 100% CPU. The ReDoS originates one repository down, in Rack. At tag v3.0.3, Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges (lib/rack/utils.rb) parses each comma-separated range segment with `return nil unless range_spec =~ /(\d*)-(\d*)/`; a Range header of many `0-,` segments drives this nested-quantifier match into catastrophic backtracking, so the request thread spins forever with no exception. The real upstream fix (rack commit 7a9d76a7850455a5ef9403203ea757ed110e7806, CVE-2022-44570) replaces the regex with a linear split-based parse (`range_spec.include?('-')` then `range_spec.split('-')`). The path: Sinatra's send_file (lib/sinatra/base.rb) delegates to Rack::Files.new(...).serving; Rack::Files#serving (lib/rack/files.rb) reads the HTTP_RANGE header and calls Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges on it. The vulnerable regex lives in Rack, not Sinatra, which is why an app-level search never surfaces it.

required_files.rationale: Fix site: get_byte_ranges parses each range segment with a nested-quantifier regex `/(\d*)-(\d*)/` at v3.0.3, which backtracks catastrophically on crafted multi-segment Range input. Real upstream fix (commit 7a9d76a7, CVE-2022-44570) replaces it with a split-based linear parse.
Rack::Files#serving reads the incoming HTTP_RANGE header and calls Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges on it; the hop inside Rack that carries the attacker header into the vulnerable utility.
send_file constructs a Rack::Files server and calls serving(request, path), delegating range handling to Rack; the cross-repo boundary the investigator must cross from the app's only call.
